$comment: Access labels for examples/corpus, declared beside the corpus rather than inside it.
It sits outside the crawl root on purpose: a label file inside the corpus would be ingested,
chunked and retrievable — an access-control policy answering questions about itself. Keeping
it out also keeps ADR 0003 true, since bytes decide a version's identity and a label change
must not mint a new version.
There is no catch-all rule and there is not going to be one. A path no rule covers fails the
fetch for that source (ACL_UNRESOLVED) rather than acquiring a default, because a default is
how 'unknown' becomes 'public' (PRD 6.1). Adding a document to this corpus means deciding who
may read it, in this file, in the same change.
